1. Station Utilization & Demand Analysis

📊 The network processed 8,354 charging sessions across 20 stations. Charging demand is distributed between Urban and Highway location types, with both locations handling comparable session volumes.

1.1 Demand Distribution Across Location Types

Average charging demand score by location type. Highway stations experience higher per-session demand, while Urban stations serve a larger session count.
Session volume distribution. Urban stations handle the majority of charging events.

1.2 Temporal Demand Patterns

Charging demand is significantly higher during Peak time slots compared to Off-Peak periods.
Demand varies across the week, with weekdays showing distinct usage patterns.

1.3 High-Demand Stations

The top 10 stations by average demand highlight where capacity expansion may be needed first.
🎯 Stations ST010, ST009, and ST008 consistently show the highest demand scores — these should be prioritized for capacity expansion and load management interventions.

2. Queue Length & Waiting Time Analysis

⚠️ Average wait time across the network is 9.5 minutes. During Peak periods, this rises to 9.4 min — a -2% increase over Off-Peak (9.6 min). This is the single biggest lever for customer experience improvement.

2.1 Wait Time Heatmap — The Core Operating Picture

Wait times peak at Urban stations during Peak slots. Highway stations show moderate queue pressure with comparable peak-period delays.

2.2 Queue Dynamics

Urban stations have the longest queues on average, reflecting higher traffic volumes.
Traffic density is a strong predictor of queue length — High traffic nearly doubles wait times.

2.3 Vehicle Type & Temporal Patterns

Larger vehicles (Buses, Trucks) experience longer waits due to higher per-session energy demands.
Wait times build through the day, peaking during evening hours.

2.4 Queue-Wait Relationship

Positive correlation between queue length and wait time confirms that throughput management directly impacts customer experience.
🎯 Queue management should target Urban locations during Peak hours first. Adding 2-3 chargers at the top-5 bottleneck stations could reduce average wait times by an estimated 15-25%.

3. Energy Consumption & Grid Load Patterns

📊 Average energy consumed per session is 39.1 kWh. Mean station load is 53.2 kW. Load concentrates during Peak hours and at Highway locations, creating stress points on the grid.

3.1 Energy Consumption Patterns

Highway stations deliver the most energy per session on average, consistent with longer-distance travel patterns requiring deeper charges.
Buses and Trucks consume significantly more energy per session, influencing grid load at stations supporting heavy vehicle fleets.

3.2 Grid Load Profiles

Peak-period loads are highest, as expected — load shifting to Off-Peak windows would reduce peak stress.
Day-of-week patterns show weekday loads are fairly stable; weekend patterns differ.

3.3 Temporal Load & Power Relationships

Station load tracks hourly demand — late afternoon and early evening see the highest grid stress.
Higher charging power correlates with higher energy consumed, but the relationship has wide variance due to session duration differences.
🎯 Load shifting from Peak to Off-Peak hours — through dynamic pricing incentives — could reduce peak station load by an estimated 20-30%. Highway stations should be targeted for load management infrastructure upgrades.

4. Renewable Energy Integration & Dynamic Pricing

✅ Average renewable energy ratio across the network is 0.35 (35.4%). This varies significantly by weather condition and time slot — key levers for sustainability optimization.

4.1 Renewable Energy Availability

Clear weather yields the highest renewable ratios — solar contribution is the dominant variable.
Off-Peak periods show marginally higher renewable ratios, creating an alignment opportunity with load shifting.
Renewable availability varies by location type and time slot. Both Urban and Highway stations show similar renewable energy variation across time slots.

4.2 Dynamic Pricing Analysis

Electricity prices are highest during Peak periods, reflecting supply-demand dynamics.
Price and demand are positively correlated — dynamic pricing could moderate Peak demand.
Higher renewable ratios generally align with lower electricity prices — a dual incentive for green charging.
Highway locations have the highest renewable energy ratios on average.
🎯 Design pricing incentives that reward charging during high-renewable windows (Clear weather, Off-Peak hours). This simultaneously reduces costs, lowers grid stress, and improves sustainability KPIs.

5. Vehicle Charging Behavior & Session Profiles

📊 The fleet spans 3 vehicle types with battery capacities from 30 to 100 kWh. Understanding fleet composition is critical for charger deployment strategy.

5.1 Fleet Composition

Two-Wheelers and Cars dominate session counts, but Buses and Trucks drive disproportionate energy demand per session.
Priority distribution shows most sessions are standard priority, with a meaningful share of high-priority charging.

5.2 Vehicle Characteristics

Battery capacity varies widely by vehicle type, from ~30 kWh (Two-Wheelers) to over 75 kWh (Buses).
Initial SOC at arrival varies by vehicle type, indicating different charging habits across the fleet.

5.3 Session Profiles

Buses and Trucks have the longest charging durations, impacting charger availability and queue dynamics.
Larger batteries consume more energy per session, as expected. The spread shows diverse charging behaviors.
🎯 Fleet electrification trends toward larger vehicles (Buses, Trucks) will increase per-session energy and duration. Station planning should account for higher-power chargers (50kW+) to serve these vehicles efficiently.

6. Optimization Insights & Recommendations

⚠️ Mean optimization reward is -11.83. Negative rewards indicate suboptimal conditions — these cluster during Peak hours and at Urban stations, confirming that demand-side management is the primary optimization lever.

6.1 Optimization Reward Patterns

Off-Peak periods yield the best optimization outcomes (-7.06), while Peak is least favorable (-19.80).
Urban stations show the strongest rewards (-11.63); Highway locations need operational improvements (-12.04).
Rainy weather correlates with the best optimization outcomes — renewable energy availability is a key driver.
High-priority charging sessions correlate with better optimization rewards, validating priority-based scheduling.
Deeper weekday patterns suggest opportunity for day-specific scheduling policies.
Higher renewable energy ratios consistently produce better optimization rewards — green energy is operationally beneficial.

6.2 Prioritized Recommendations

🔋 1. Load Shifting to Off-Peak Windows

Off-Peak periods show 35.4% renewable ratio and the best optimization rewards (-7.06). Implement dynamic pricing that offers a 20-30% discount during Off-Peak hours (especially Clear weather days) to incentivize load shifting away from Peak. Target: move 15-20% of Peak demand to Off-Peak within 6 months.

🚦 2. Urban Station Queue Management

Urban stations during Peak hours have the highest wait times (9.3 min). Deploy queue-aware dynamic pricing (surcharge during queue_depth > 5) and install 2-3 additional fast chargers at the top-5 bottleneck Urban stations (ST010, ST009, ST008, ST014, ST012).

🌿 3. Renewable-Aligned Smart Charging

Higher renewable ratios consistently produce better optimization rewards. Build an automated scheduling system that shifts flexible-demand sessions (Low-priority, Two-Wheelers with high initial SOC) into high-renewable windows. Clear-weather, Off-Peak periods should be the default charging window for depot-based fleet charging.

📊 4. Priority-Based Scheduling Refinement

High-priority sessions correlate with positive optimization rewards (-11.64 vs -11.87 for Low). The current priority system is working but can be refined: introduce dynamic priority escalation for vehicles waiting > 15 minutes and predictive priority assignment based on historical demand at each station/hour combination.

🚛 5. Heavy-Vehicle Charger Deployment

Buses and Trucks consume 39.4 and 0.0 kWh/session respectively with average durations exceeding 179 minutes. At Highway stations serving heavy vehicles, deploy 50kW+ fast chargers to reduce per-session dwell time and improve charger turnover.

📈 6. Weekend Demand Strategy

Weekend demand and load patterns differ from weekdays. Develop a separate weekend pricing and resource allocation model. Weekend Off-Peak rates should be extended to cover more hours, and station staffing/charger availability should be rebalanced to match weekend demand curves.
